issues.legal_issue: Criminal proceedings may be quashed under the court’s inherent powers when the allegations, even taken at face value, do not prima facie disclose an offence.
Criminal proceedings may be quashed when the uncontroverted allegations and supporting evidence do not disclose the commission of an offence.
Criminal proceedings may be quashed when the allegations are absurd and inherently improbable.
Criminal proceedings may be quashed when they are manifestly malicious and instituted with an ulterior motive to wreak vengeance arising from a private dispute.
Continuing criminal proceedings that are maliciously instituted and unsupported by the allegations constitutes an abuse of the process of law.
